In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPDs connected to overhead distribution lines can effectively suppress the lightning current and voltage, and thus protect the line and its equipment from damage caused by lightning.
, when a nearby return stroke is involved, the SPDs connected to an overhead line can be damaged if the average gradient of the return stroke current is greater than 2.5 kA/μs.
, in general, SPDs connected to power lines can be expected to survive nearby lightning strikes, but the residual voltage and current flow through them may be significant and should not be ignored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lightning-induced overvoltage on SPD connected to an overhead line is mainly caused by the return strokes, which are the main cause of the SPD residual voltages and currents.
SPD can effectively limit the overvoltages and currents on overhead power lines due to lightning.
the SPD with a low nominal discharge current can withstand a lightning current of 10 kA, and the SPD can be used for the overhead distribution lines.
